title: Projectile Pierce, Fork, Chain, and Return in Path of Exile 2
summary: How Pierce, Fork, Chain, and Return resolve on a single projectile collision in Path of Exile 2, including the priority order, enemy vs terrain chaining, and which skills forbid certain behaviours.
description: A mechanics guide to Path of Exile 2 projectile behaviours: the collision priority order (Split, Pierce, Fork, Chain, Return), how enemy-chain differs from terrain-chain, which skills cannot Pierce/Fork/Chain/Return, and how to pick supports for clearing vs bossing.
imageAlt: A Path of Exile 2 support gem icon representing projectile chain behaviour
prerequisites: Basic understanding of projectile skills and support gems
Familiarity with the in-game tooltip and the stats panel
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: What is the collision priority order for projectile behaviours?
body: Whenever a projectile collides, it checks its remaining behaviours in this priority: Split, then Pierce, then Fork, then Chain, then Return. Only one behaviour can occur on a single collision, so the first one it still has available wins.

items.title: Can a projectile Pierce and Fork or Chain on the same hit?
body: No. Only one behaviour applies per collision. A projectile that Pierces does not Fork or Chain from that enemy; Fork/Chain from enemies only become possible after Piercing and Forking are exhausted.

items.title: Do all projectile skills support all four behaviours?
body: No. Some skills or items explicitly forbid a behaviour. For example, Lightning Arrow cannot Chain (including from terrain), and Freezing Pulse Pierces all targets so it cannot Fork. Always read the skill tooltip.

items.title: Does Return let a projectile hit the same enemy again?
body: Unlike the other behaviours, Return allows one extra collision per simultaneous set against targets that were already hit. A projectile normally Returns only once.

sections.title: Definitions
paragraphs: Projectile behaviours are special properties a projectile can carry. They decide what happens when the projectile hits an enemy or an obstacle instead of simply stopping. Four of them are the focus of this guide: Pierce, Fork, Chain, and Return. A fifth, Split, shares the same priority system and is described for completeness.

These behaviours are usually added by support gems (Pierce Support, Fork Support, Chain Support, Returning Projectiles Support) but can also come from a skill's own text, unique items, or passives. They are not all compatible on a single hit — only one resolves per collision.
bullets: Projectile: an entity that travels independently until it collides with an enemy, an obstacle, or reaches its travel limit (about 15 metres).
Pierce: the projectile passes through the enemy it hits and continues on its original trajectory. This still counts as a hit.
Fork: the projectile splits into two identical projectiles that travel away from each other at 60 and -60 degrees from the original path.
Chain: the projectile is redirected to another nearby enemy after colliding, up to a number of times.
Return: the projectile travels back toward its origin after reaching the end of its travel.
Split: the projectile splits into several auto-targeting projectiles (highest priority; only once).

sections.title: What happens on a single collision
sections.caption: Priority the game uses at each collision. It checks behaviours top to bottom and applies the first one the projectile still has available. Only one line is used per collision.

cells.on-collision: Projectile checks whether it can still Split
cells.what-happens: It splits into auto-targeting projectiles and the collision is consumed
cells.note: Highest priority; a projectile can only Split once

cells.on-collision: If Split is exhausted, it checks Pierce
cells.what-happens: Passes through the target and keeps its original trajectory
cells.note: Counts as a hit; does not change direction or speed; uses one Pierce count

cells.on-collision: If neither Split nor Pierce applies here, it checks Fork
cells.what-happens: Splits into two projectiles at 60 and -60 degrees from the path
cells.note: Only one fork unless Awakened Fork Support; a piercing hit does not fork

cells.on-collision: If still nothing applied, it checks Chain
cells.what-happens: Redirects to another enemy within about 6 metres
cells.note: Applied last among enemy-targeting behaviours; same enemy not hit twice in one Chain

cells.on-collision: If nothing else applies, or at end of travel
cells.what-happens: The projectile heads back toward its origin
cells.note: Lowest priority; normally once; allows one extra hit on already-hit targets

sections.note: This priority is the global rule in Path of Exile 2. Specific skills or unique items can override part of it (for example forcing Fork before Pierce), so never assume a single skill's special case is the universal order.

sections.title: Behaviour pairing matrix
sections.caption: Which behaviours can combine, and how. 'Per collision' means on a single hit; several behaviours can still appear across the projectile's whole journey.

cells.result: Mutually exclusive per collision. A piercing projectile does not fork on that hit; Fork only happens once Pierce is used up (or never, if it pierces all targets).
A projectile that can Pierce will not chain from enemies. It can chain from terrain after piercing.
Fork consumes the collision. After forked projectiles travel out, they may chain from terrain; enemy-chain follows only once their travel ends.
Forked projectiles can Return toward the origin at the end of their travel.
After piercing, the projectile can Return. Some uniques require a pierce condition before Return triggers.
Once the chain ends, Return can trigger and bring the projectile back.
Split has top priority and can be followed by the rest in sequence across the projectile's full path.

sections.note: Shotgun prevention still applies: when several projectiles are created at once, only one may collide with the same target, so extra copies can pass through without hitting.

sections.title: Chain from enemy vs chain from terrain
sections.caption: Enemy-target Chain and terrain/object Chain are separate systems with different rules. Do not conflate them.

cells.trigger-source: Enemy collision, projectile can Pierce or Fork
cells.notes: Only one behaviour per collision. If it pierces or forks, the enemy-chain is skipped.
Redirects to another enemy within about 6 metres; the same enemy is not targeted twice in one Chain.
By default only once unless otherwise stated. Chance to chain from terrain stacks additively. Can occur after piercing or forking an enemy.

cells.trigger-source: Skill that cannot chain (e.g. Lightning Arrow)
cells.chains-from: Does NOT chain from terrain either
cells.notes: Some skills are forbidden from chaining entirely, including off terrain. This was fixed as a bug for Lightning Arrow in patch 0.2.0.

sections.note: Projectiles have a base chaining distance of about 6 metres; other (non-projectile) effects chain from about 4 metres.

sections.title: Worked examples
sections.caption: Qualitative cases showing how the priority order and target availability change the outcome. No exact numbers are stated because support values are version-sensitive.

cells.setup: Five enemies in a row; projectile has Pierce and Chain
cells.result: The projectile Pierces through the line first (Pierce beats Chain). After Pierce is used up with no more enemies in the way, it may chain from terrain or simply end. Chain from enemies does not trigger while it can still Pierce.

cells.setup: One enemy near a wall; projectile has % chance to chain from terrain
cells.result: On hitting the enemy with no Pierce/Fork left, the projectile can chain off the wall to a second enemy. Terrain chain happens at most once by default and its chance is additive.

cells.setup: One boss; projectile has Fork, Chain, and Return
cells.result: With no other target nearby, Fork and Chain find nothing to redirect to and travel off. Return can add one extra collision against the boss (the only already-hit target), making Return the most useful of the four here.

sections.note: These are teaching examples of the priority system. Exact Pierce/Chain counts and damage come from the current in-game tooltip.

sections.title: Clear speed vs bossing
sections.intro: Pick the kind of encounter you are building for. The tool points to the supports that actually help.

rules.title: Spread damage for clear speed
steps: Use Chain and/or Fork to reach extra enemies that the single projectile would miss.
Add Pierce if enemies are lined up so one shot passes through several.
Remember only one behaviour per collision: Fork or Chain, not both, on a given hit.

rules.title: Focus the single target
steps: Prefer Pierce plus Return, since Return can add one extra hit on the same boss.
Fork and Chain give little on a lone enemy because they need other targets to redirect to.
If the boss is the only target, most of a Fork/Chain setup is wasted travel.

defaultResult.title: General support choice
steps: Match the support to the target density you fight most.
Use Fork/Chain for packs, Pierce/Return for single targets.
Check the in-game tooltip for current counts and damage modifiers.

sections.title: Skills and items that forbid behaviours
paragraphs: Not every projectile skill can use all four behaviours. Some skills or items explicitly forbid one, and the rule is written in the skill or item text. Always read the tooltip before assuming a support will work.

In general, a behaviour is forbidden when the text says the projectile 'cannot Pierce / Fork / Chain / Return', or when the skill already has a built-in behaviour that blocks another (for example a skill that Pierces all targets cannot Fork on a hit it passes through).
bullets: Lightning Arrow: cannot Chain, including off terrain (fixed as a bug in patch 0.2.0).
Freezing Pulse: projectiles Pierce all targets, so they cannot Fork.
Spectral Throw: projectiles Return and behave as piercing, so Fork does not apply on its hits.
Some unique items (for example the Snakepit ring) prevent spell projectiles from Piercing or Chaining depending on the socket.
Ascendancy or passive effects can also grant or remove a behaviour; the tooltip is the source of truth.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Most projectile problems come from misunderstanding the priority order and the single-behaviour-per-collision rule rather than from bad rolls. Watch for these before blaming the game.
bullets: Chain 'not triggering': the projectile can also Pierce or Fork, so enemy-chain is skipped; or there is no valid enemy within the chain distance; or the skill cannot chain at all.
Projectile 'disappears': it ran out of behaviours and travelled off. Fork and Chain need a valid secondary target, otherwise the projectile just expires at its travel limit.
Return 'deals no damage': shotgun prevention means a returning projectile gets only one extra collision per set on already-hit targets; other returns pass through without colliding.
Assuming every projectile skill supports all four behaviours — check the tooltip for 'cannot Pierce/Fork/Chain/Return'.
Conflating enemy Chain with terrain Chain — they follow different rules and limits.
Mixing up Fork (two at plus/minus 60 degrees) with Split (auto-targeting copies) and with Projectile Count (more separate projectiles).

sections.title: Common points of confusion
sections.intro: Paraphrased confusions players often raise about projectile behaviours.

cards.title: Chain feels weak on bosses
body: Players expect Chain to add damage to a lone boss, but Chain needs another enemy to redirect to. On a single target it does almost nothing, which is the core point of the referenced video guide.
cards.linkLabel: Why Chain Might Be Worse Than You Think

cards.title: Pierce and Fork together
body: Many assume a gem can both Pierce and Fork on the same hit. Only one behaviour resolves per collision, so a piercing hit does not fork.

cards.title: Lightning Arrow still chains
body: Some players believed Lightning Arrow could chain off terrain. Patch 0.2.0 fixed it so the skill cannot chain at all, including off terrain.

cards.title: Return hitting the same enemy
body: Players are surprised a returning projectile hits an already-hit enemy again. Return uniquely allows one extra collision per set on targets already struck.

items.question: Can every projectile skill use Pierce, Fork, Chain, and Return?
answer: No. Some skills or items explicitly forbid a behaviour. Lightning Arrow cannot Chain (including from terrain), and Freezing Pulse Pierces all targets so it cannot Fork. Read the skill tooltip for 'cannot Pierce/Fork/Chain/Return'.

items.question: What is the priority order when a projectile collides?
answer: The game checks Split, then Pierce, then Fork, then Chain, then Return. Only one of these behaviours occurs on a single collision, so the first one the projectile still has available wins.

items.question: Does Chain from enemies work the same as Chain from terrain?
answer: No. If the projectile can Pierce or Fork, it will not chain from enemies, but it can chain from terrain afterward (and only once by default). Some skills cannot chain from terrain either.

items.question: Does Return hit the same enemy again?
answer: Yes. Unlike the other behaviours, Return allows one extra collision per simultaneous set against targets that were already hit. A projectile normally Returns only once.

items.question: What is the base chain distance?
answer: Projectiles chain from about 6 metres away; other (non-projectile) effects chain from about 4 metres. The same enemy is not targeted twice within one Chain.

items.question: Is Fork the same as Split or Projectile Count?
answer: No. Fork makes two projectiles at 60 and -60 degrees. Split makes several auto-targeting copies. Projectile Count simply fires more separate projectiles. Shotgun prevention still stops multiple simultaneous projectiles from all hitting one target.
